articles.title: The Hatch Restore 2 is the secret to my early mornings
articles.summary: The Hatch Restore 2 is the best sunrise alarm clock and sound machine. We tried it for four months to learn what’s different about the Hatch Restore vs. Restore 2.
articles.body: Since getting my first iPhone over a decade ago, buying an alarm clock has felt unnecessary. I did not see a reason to spend money on a separate device when there’s a free app pre-installed on my phone. I now realize that being startled awake by a blaring ringing noise is a terrible way to start my day. Plus, keeping my phone next to my bed offered too much of a temptation to answer one last email or watch one last TikTok before dozing off. The solution was obvious, though it came in the form of a product I’d sworn off: an alarm clock. But not just any alarm clock. My research led me to the Hatch Restore 2, a customizable sunrise alarm clock that uses light and sound to guide users awake. It also acts as a sound machine, night light and clock. Now that I’ve used it for months, I can safely say that the Hatch Restore 2 (which the brand sent me to try) has altered my sleep for the better. I no longer dread waking up because I have the device’s beautiful lightscape and serene noises to look forward to, and listening to relaxing river sounds calms my mind as it lulls me to sleep. Below, I’ll share my experience trying the Hatch Restore 2 and why I think it’s worth investing in, regardless of what type of sleeper you are. SKIP AHEAD What is the Hatch Restore 2? | How I tried the Hatch Restore 2 | My experience with the Hatch Restore 2 | Potential drawbacks to keep in mind | Who is the Hatch Restore 2 best for? What is the Hatch Restore 2? The Hatch Restore 2 ($199.99) is a cross between a sunrise alarm clock and a sound machine. If you’re unfamiliar with a sunrise alarm clock, it’s a device that mimics a sunrise by gradually emitting light up to an hour before your scheduled wake-up time. Sunrise alarm clocks gently encourage you out of your slumber instead of suddenly jolting you awake like standard alarm clocks do. Many also pair their sunrise with a peaceful sound like wind chimes or chirping birds to further coax you out of bed. Hatch Restore 2 Sunrise alarm clocks give your body time to react and adjust to leaving the sleep state and entering the wake state, according to Dr. Christopher Winter, a neurologist and sleep specialist. The Hatch Restore 2, which is available in three colors including Slate (gray), Latte (tan) and Putty (white), takes that peaceful wake-up experience a step further by allowing you to fully customize its settings. The linen-covered device pairs with a free companion app (iOS or Android) via Wi-Fi, through which you can schedule up to 15 individual sunrise alarms along with 13 calming alarm sounds like morning birds and wind chimes. For each alarm, you choose the light color and brightness level for the sunrise, as well as the sound and its volume level. You also choose the sunrise duration, what time you want the alarm to go off and what days of the week you want the alarm to repeat. You can also set alarms with just a sunrise or just a sound, if you prefer. For example, if you want to be fully awake by 6:30 a.m. and set the sunrise duration to be an hour, the light starts gradually getting brighter at 5:30 a.m. It will reach its most intense brightness at 6:30 a.m., which is also what time the noise sounds. You can also toggle alarms on or off depending on when you want to use them. I set a weekday alarm and a weekend alarm, but toggle the weekday alarm off instead of deleting it if I have a day off or it’s a holiday. The Hatch Restore 2 doesn’t just aim to ease you into your morning — it also helps lull you to sleep. You can program up to five unique sounds to use at night, like white noise, ocean waves and rain., and can choose each one’s duration and volume, plus whether you want to pair it with a night light. You can also program night lights without any noise if you just want to softly illuminate your room while sleeping. Unlike the sunrise alarm clock, you cannot schedule the sound machine or nightlight to start at a specific time, so you have to either turn it on via the Hatch app or by pressing a button on the device. However, you can set a rest reminder through the app, which sends a push notification to your phone at a specific time and on days you select, nudging to start heading you to bed. The Hatch is also a digital clock. Through the app, you can choose to keep the clock on or off at all times, or turn it off at night. You can also set your preferences for the clock’s daytime and nighttime brightness levels in the app or on the machine itself. How I tried the Hatch Restore 2 In 2022, I received the Hatch Restore, the brand’s original model, as a holiday gift from my family and used it for a year until the new model came out. Up until that point I had been using my iPhone as an alarm clock. After the Restore 2 came out in 2023, the brand sent me it to try, and I’ve been using it for about four months in my New York City apartment, where I am the only one using the device. I typically wake up around 6:15 a.m. on weekdays and 8:30 a.m. on weekends. I’ve slept with a sound machine on at night for as long as I can remember and cannot sleep without one. Because everyone’s sleep and wake habits are different, I asked five NBC Selected staffers to try and share their feedback about the Restore 2. The brand sent SEO editor Nikki Brown, associate SEO reporter Ashley Morris, editor Cory Fernandez, and former production coordinator Kelsey Fredricks the device — they’ve been using it for a little over a month. Former associate reporter Bianca Alvarez bought the Restore 2 herself in 2023 and has been using it for about four months as well. All of my fellow testers have never used a sunrise alarm clock or Hatch product prior to trying the Restore 2. They all sleep alone, so, like me, they’re the only ones using the devices in their homes. My experience with the Hatch Restore 2 When my colleagues and I came together to debrief about our experiences, we unanimously agreed that it revolutionized our sleep. Below, I’ll share more details about my experience using the Restore 2. Setup and design Setting up the Restore 2 is a very straightforward process because the companion app walks you through every step. I followed its prompts to connect the device to Wi-Fi, give it a name and start customizing my rise and rest routines. Since the curved device has a sleek, minimalist appearance, it practically blends into my bedroom. The buttons are also flush with the top of the device, so they do not draw attention to themselves. I also appreciate that the Restore 2 comes in three linen colors, allowing me to choose the one that best fits my bedroom decor. Sunrise alarm clock It only took one sleep for me to understand how much of an impact a gentle wake-up call has on my morning. I wake up at 6:15 a.m. during the week to run before work, and my iPhone alarm would always make me jump. It was such an unpleasant experience to have at the start of my day, and I often found myself waking up in the middle of the night to check the time because I dreaded being woken up so abruptly. But that sense of dread has gone away since I started using the Restore 2, and I’m more likely to sleep through the night now since I’m not anticipating being startled awake. The gradual increase of light in my bedroom lets me slowly transition from a deep sleep into consciousness. Another benefit of using the sunrise alarm clock is that it’s hard to ignore, says Alvarez. She previously used her iPhone as an alarm, but frequently slept through it because the volume was too low or she forgot to turn the volume on so her phone just vibrated. But the Restore 2 pairs light and sound to wake you up — together, those two cues are almost impossible to sleep through, she says. And while you can hit snooze on the device, it just stops the noise for nine minutes, which means the bright light still illuminates your room. I find it hard to fall back asleep when I’ve already seen a bright light, so while I may snooze the sound on my Restore 2 once in a while, it just briefly delays me from getting out of bed. Being able to customize the sunrise I want to experience is one of the best parts about the Restore 2. I love scrolling through the different sound and light options to find a combination that works for my mood that week. Sound machine and nightlight Prior to using the Restore 2, I relied on the same Homedics noise machine for years and was quite attached to it. I found the sound soothing and knew what my perfect volume level was, so I was worried that I would have a hard time adjusting to using a new noise machine. Now, however, I cannot imagine not dozing off while listening to the Restore 2’s relaxing river sound at a 24% volume level. The Restore 2’s three speakers make me feel immersed in the crisp, full noise more so than other sound machines I’ve used. And with over 20 noises to choose from, I was able to experiment with different options and really think about which one created a peaceful atmosphere in my bedroom. The Hatch app also remembers my ideal volume level, so I don’t have to fiddle with the settings every night. While I do not use the night light feature, many of my fellow testers do: Fernandez turns on its dim night light before bed when he doesn’t want it to be completely dark yet, and Morris customizes the color of her night light depending on what she’s watching as part of her nighttime routine. Alvarez also programs one to keep her accountable about going to sleep at a reasonable hour. “Sometimes I’ll be working at night or watching TV and realize it’s getting too late, so I pick one of the sunsets and set it for an hour, that way I know when it turns off, it’s time for bed,” she says. The night light makes a great reading light, too. Potential drawbacks to keep in mind Requires a Wi-Fi connection To set up and use the Restore 2, it needs a Wi-Fi connection at all times. My fellow reviewers found that the location of their Wi-Fi router in relation to their Restore 2 impacted their ability to use the device. “The Wi-Fi in my bedroom wasn’t strong enough for the initial connection to work,” says Morris. “Once I checked the instructions, I saw that they suggested setting up the Restore 2 close to the router. I plugged it in beside my router and it worked immediately.” Additionally, if the Wi-Fi or power goes out in your home, you won’t be able to use the Restore 2. If this were to happen overnight, you might not wake up on time. Fredricks says she sets a secondary alarm on her phone just in case. But requiring a Wi-Fi connection is par for the course with most other customizable sunrise alarm clocks as well, like the Loftie Clock, WiiM Wake-Up Light and Philips SmartSleep Sleep and Wake-Up Light. Must remain plugged in Since the Restore 2 has to be connected to an outlet at all times, it’s not particularly suitable for traveling, but Brown wishes it was. The cord is also on the shorter side, which limits where you can set it up. Reliant on the Hatch app The only way to set up alarms and sound machines on the Restore 2 is through the Hatch sleep app, so you must have an iPhone or Android to use the device and cannot manually change its settings via the buttons on the device. However, after you schedule sunrise alarm clocks, noise machines and/or night lights, you can turn them on and off using the built-in buttons. So long as the Restore 2 is plugged in, connected to Wi-Fi and connected to the Hatch app, it displays the time. The device’s clock syncs to the clock on your phone, which means it automatically adjusts itself during daylight saving time and if you move to a new time zone. Who is the Hatch Restore 2 best for? Generally speaking, almost everyone can benefit from incorporating the Hatch Restore 2 into their sleep routine. My fellow reviewers and I each have different rise and wind down preferences, but we all found that the Restore 2 made our bedtime routines and morning routines more enjoyable, peaceful and easier to stick to. More specifically, anyone who dreads being jolted awake by the alarm on their phone will appreciate the Restore 2. “This has been a game changer for me,” says Brown. “The difference between waking up to a gradual sunrise and calming sounds, and my iPhone alarm is huge. I haven’t needed to hit the snooze button once since I started using it, even after nights when I didn’t get a lot of sleep. I feel way more refreshed and alert. Meet our experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Christopher Winter is a neurologist and sleep specialist based in Charlottesville, Virginia. Why trust NBC Selected? Zoe Malin is an associate updates editor for NBC Selected who covers sleep products like sleep masks, silk pajamas and weighted stuffed animals. For this article, she tried the Hatch Restore 2, which the brand sent her and five other NBC Selected staff members to try. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Why should I care if share prices fall?
articles.summary: Changes in the FTSE 100 and other indexes are not just for financial experts, they can affect our lives.
articles.body:
Major tech firms have seen their stock values fall after a sell-off by investors following the US midterm elections.

The fall in the value of their shares across the world has been blamed on an expectation of a slowdown in AI development, although it comes after sharp rises over recent years.

As companies grow, they may issue shares. Many of the largest companies in the UK have shares which are bought and sold on the London Stock Exchange.

Their collective performance is often quoted amid a blizzard of numbers that may feel confusing and irrelevant.

Booms or falls in the stock market make the news, but rarely does anyone mention the FTSE 100 during a coffee with friends.

Yet, there are good reasons why this performance affects your life and finances.

'I don't invest' - actually, you probably do

Many people's initial reaction to "the markets" is that they are not directly affected, because they do not invest money.

Yet there are millions of people with a pension - either private or through work - who will see their savings (in what is known as a defined contribution pension) invested by pension schemes. The value of their savings pot is influenced by the performance of these investments.

Pension savers mostly let experts choose where to invest this money to help it grow. Widespread falls in share prices are likely to be bad news for pension savers.

Hundreds of billions of pounds are held in defined contribution pensions at the moment.

So big rises or falls can affect your pension, but the advice is to remember that pension savings, like any investments, are usually a long-term bet.

Experts say that investors have always had to ride economic shocks. Investments, by definition, require a long-term outlook and strategy. So, they are urging people not to panic in such circumstances or make knee-jerk decisions.

Some people have a pension which promises a specific value, depending on their salary. Others have no pension at all.

Millions of people have been automatically enrolled into a pension and may have not really noticed. Those schemes see employers divert wages into a pension and contribute some money themselves. The government adds a little in tax relief.

In every case, the value of these pension savings is affected by investment performance. So "the markets" matter - maybe not as much as everyday wages, but for future pensions.

What happens if I'm just about to retire?

Timing is more critical for those at retirement age, as this may be when a retiree uses their pension pot to buy a retirement income, or annuity. The bigger the pot, the more income they will get in retirement.

As you approach retirement age, pension pots tend to be moved to less risky investments, such as government bonds. When stock markets fall, these bonds can do better.

Anyone who has a pension pot invested and is taking an income from it will again see their investment go up and down with the stock markets.

That could mean getting less than you expected if you cash in too much after stock markets have fallen, making it important to plan how to make up any of this shortfall, experts say.

However, higher interest rates tend to mean better rates offered on annuities, and there is a chance of more rate rises in the UK by the Bank of England.

If share prices fall for an extended period then that could have an effect on jobs.

That's because investors in the company expect a return on that investment.

When it falls for a while, then they would expect the business to address issues, for example by cutting costs, and therefore jobs.

There is a huge element of the unknown here though. Companies have to consider lots of factors when making decisions on investment and employment.

In purely investment terms, lower share prices can offer an opportunity to buy, in the hope that over the long term, they recover and rise. Many people will do this initially through a stocks and shares Individual Savings Account (Isa).

However, it is worth noting that the sell-off in tech stocks in particular came after big rises, so long-term investors are still likely to have seen gains.

Experts and regulators are at pains to point out that investments can go down as well as up, and urge people not to put everything into one investment, but to diversify.

Some people invest money in what are known as tracker funds. These go up and down in line with the performance of a certain index, such as the FTSE 100.

So if the index falls, so does the value of their investments and vice versa. One advantage of these funds is that they often cost relatively little to sign up to.

Yes, and millions of people do, but experts stress that a long-term strategy is required to ride out short-term falls. It is also important to ensure cash savings are held too, so unexpected expenses - like the need for a replacement boiler - can be covered.

The government is keen to get people in the UK to invest more, partly because it says that will help UK economic growth and partly because it is much more popular among individuals in the US and some parts of Europe.

It backed an advertising campaign to encourage people to invest, funded by some of the UK's biggest financial services firms.

But the choice of "Savvy the Squirrel" to front the campaign has raised some eyebrows. Some question whether the push could get anywhere close to the success of the Tell Sid adverts of the 1980s, which encouraged people to invest in the newly privatised British Gas.

When we see big shifts in the stock markets there can also be fluctuations in the value of currencies and exchange rates.

As a result, prices could go up, but could also go down.

Upheaval to economies across the world, to oil prices and so on, have a big impact on what we pay at home for goods and services, so there are lots of factors in play.

articles.title: Rafael Fonteles anuncia permanência de controladora-geral no próximo mandato | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Governo do Piauí, Maria do Amparo Esmério Silva é auditora governamental de carreira.
articles.summary: Segundo o Governo do Piauí, Maria do Amparo Esmério Silva é auditora governamental de carreira.
articles.body:
O governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), anunciou nesta sexta-feira (6) a permanência de Maria do Amparo Esmério Silva no comando da Controladoria-Geral do Estado (CGE) no próximo mandato.

Rafael Fonteles também confirmou a permanência dos secretários Dirceu Campelo (Saúde), Antônio Luiz (Segurança Pública), Rodrigo Torres (Educação), Emílio Júnior (Fazenda), Washington Bonfim (Planejamento) e Núbia Lopes (Relações Sociais) nos cargos que ocupam atualmente.

"Nossa gratidão por aceitar a renovação dessa missão tão importante para a eficiência e transparência das políticas públicas do Estado do Piauí", escreveu o governador no anúncio.

Segundo o Governo do Piauí, Maria do Amparo Esmério Silva é auditora governamental de carreira e já comandou a Controladoria-Geral do Estado (CGE) entre 2006 e 2010. Ao longo da trajetória no serviço público, também ocupou os cargos de gerente de Convênios e de Pessoal e Previdência.

Maria do Amparo Esmério Silva, Controladora-Geral do Estado do Piauí — Foto: Governo do Piauí

Rafael Fonteles começou a anunciar o secretariado para o novo mandato mesmo em meio a especulações sobre uma eventual participação na equipe ministerial do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

O nome de Rafael passou a ser citado em especulações após a atuação na coordenação da campanha petista durante o segundo turno.

O governador reeleito do Piauí negou repetidas vezes que tenha discutido com Lula a possibilidade de assumir um cargo no governo federal e afirmou que pretende cumprir o mandato para o qual foi reeleito.

articles.title: Concurso do IBGE oferta mais de 500 vagas para o Tocantins | G1
articles.standfirst: Selecionados vão atuar no Censo Agropecuário de 2027 e terão direito a salário e benefícios. Inscrições vão até 25 de novembro pela Fundação Cesgranrio.
articles.summary: Selecionados vão atuar no Censo Agropecuário de 2027 e terão direito a salário e benefícios. Inscrições vão até 25 de novembro pela Fundação Cesgranrio.
articles.body:
O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) abriu, nesta sexta-feira (6), as inscrições do concurso temporário para o cargo de recenseador em todo o país. No Tocantins, são 523 vagas para atuação em 107 municípios.

Os aprovados irão atuar no 12º Censo Agropecuário, Florestal e Aquícola de 2027. Os interessados podem se candidatar até 25 de novembro pelo site da Fundação Cesgranrio , organizadora da seleção. A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 70.

Conforme o edital, são ofertadas 27.279 vagas ao todo. A remuneração fixa mensal é de R$ 1.741, mas o edital prevê pagamento por produtividade, que pode elevar os ganhos para até R$ 4.370.

Além do salário, os contratados terão direito a auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192, auxílio-deslocamento, auxílio pré-escolar, férias proporcionais acrescidas de um terço e 13º salário proporcional.

IBGE Tocantins — Foto: Helena Pontes/Agência IBGE Notícias

As provas serão aplicadas no dia 31 de janeiro de 2027 , das 13h às 17h. O exame terá 60 questões, distribuídas entre Língua Portuguesa, Matemática e Conhecimentos Técnicos sobre o Censo Agropecuário.

Para ser aprovado, o candidato precisará obter pelo menos 18 pontos no total e acertar ao menos uma questão em cada disciplina.

Os contratos terão duração inicial estimada de seis meses , mas poderão ser prorrogados de acordo com a necessidade do IBGE, respeitado o limite legal de quatro anos.

Os candidatos convocados também precisarão participar de treinamento obrigatório, com aproveitamento mínimo de 60%.

Segundo o edital, os recenseadores serão responsáveis por visitar estabelecimentos agropecuários, realizar entrevistas com produtores rurais e registrar informações em dispositivos eletrônicos de coleta.

Entre os dados levantados, estarão informações sobre produção agrícola, pecuária, aquicultura, uso da terra, mão de obra e características dos estabelecimentos rurais.

As informações coletadas servirão de base para pesquisas estatísticas, formulação de políticas públicas e planejamento de ações governamentais voltadas ao setor agropecuário brasileiro.

articles.title: Por que a homologação da Anatel é importante na compra de eletrônicos | G1
articles.standfirst: Verificação do selo, da procedência e do canal de venda ajuda o consumidor a evitar equipamentos irregulares e reduzir riscos à segurança
articles.summary: Verificação do selo, da procedência e do canal de venda ajuda o consumidor a evitar equipamentos irregulares e reduzir riscos à segurança
articles.body:
Na hora de comprar um equipamento eletrônico, não basta olhar apenas para o preço, as funcionalidades ou a marca. Verificar se o produto é homologado pela Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) também é importante para evitar equipamentos irregulares e garantir que eles atendam aos requisitos técnicos de qualidade, segurança e funcionamento exigidos para a comercialização no país.

Gilberto Gandelman, CEO da Proeletronic, destaca que escolher equipamentos homologados ajuda a reduzir riscos e garante que o produto foi avaliado de acordo com as exigências aplicáveis. "A homologação é um indicativo importante de que o equipamento passou pelos procedimentos previstos para aquela categoria. Por isso, o consumidor não deve considerar apenas preço e funcionalidades na hora da compra, mas também verificar se o produto é regular e possui a homologação correspondente", explica.

A homologação também ajuda a garantir que o equipamento seja compatível com os sistemas de telecomunicações e funcione de acordo com os requisitos técnicos previstos. Por isso, antes de finalizar a compra, é importante conferir se o produto possui o selo de homologação e consultar o número correspondente na base de produtos homologados da Anatel.

Outro ponto de atenção é a procedência. Equipamentos irregulares podem chegar ao consumidor por diferentes canais, inclusive lojas físicas e plataformas de comércio eletrônico. Em fiscalizações, a Anatel identificou e retirou do mercado mais de 1,3 milhão de produtos irregulares entre janeiro de 2025 e janeiro de 2026, incluindo roteadores, equipamentos de Wi-Fi e carregadores.

Casos envolvendo aparelhos como TV Boxes reforçam a importância desse cuidado. Além de verificar a homologação, o consumidor deve observar as informações sobre fabricante, responsável pela comercialização e assistência. Equipamentos não homologados podem representar riscos à saúde e à segurança e não oferecem as mesmas garantias relacionadas aos requisitos técnicos avaliados no processo de certificação.

Comparativo entre o SmartPro original e a versão falsificada. — Foto: Divulgação

A atenção deve ser redobrada diante de ofertas que parecem vantajosas demais ou de produtos que utilizam imagens e logotipos de marcas conhecidas, como já ocorreu com versões falsificadas do SmartPro. "A falsificação pode dificultar a identificação do produto verdadeiro, principalmente quando o anúncio utiliza fotos e informações de um equipamento legítimo.

Por isso, é importante não confiar apenas na aparência. O consumidor deve verificar o selo, o número de homologação e a procedência antes de finalizar a compra", afirma Gandelman.

Para o CEO da Proeletronic, alguns cuidados simples podem ajudar a evitar problemas. "Vale conferir se o equipamento está homologado pela Anatel, consultar o número de homologação na base da Agência, verificar a procedência e dar preferência a canais de venda confiáveis. São passos rápidos que ajudam o consumidor a fazer uma compra mais segura", conclui.

Com mais de 30 anos de atuação no mercado, a Proeletronic é uma empresa brasileira especializada no desenvolvimento e na fabricação de soluções para recepção e distribuição de sinais de TV aberta e paga, além de produtos para segurança, áudio e vídeo, telefonia e internet.

A companhia possui unidades industriais em Paraisópolis (MG) e Jacareí (SP) e atua em diferentes segmentos do setor eletroeletrônico, com portfólio que inclui soluções para TV, telefonia móvel, fechaduras, pilhas e baterias, sensores de presença, cabos, suportes para TV, além de produtos voltados a provedores de internet (ISPs) e infraestrutura de fibra óptica.

A linha de fibra óptica, comercializada sob a marca TERAPRO, atende representantes, distribuidores e lojistas que atuam no mercado de provedores de internet em todo o país. Com presença em todo o território nacional por meio de uma ampla rede de distribuidores, varejistas, representantes e e-commerce, a Proeletronic também exporta seus produtos para a América Latina e a Europa.

A empresa é certificada ISO 9001 e possui certificação em conformidade com os requisitos da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD).

A atenção à experiência do consumidor também integra a atuação da Proeletronic, que em 2026 concorre ao Prêmio Reclame AQUI na categoria Eletrônicos – Fabricantes.

articles.title: Educadora física orienta iniciantes para a Corrida Unimed Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Escolha da distância, cuidados nos últimos dias e hidratação são pontos importantes para participar do evento com segurança, especialmente diante do calor da capital.
articles.summary: Escolha da distância, cuidados nos últimos dias e hidratação são pontos importantes para participar do evento com segurança, especialmente diante do calor da capital.
articles.body:
A educadora física da Unimed Teresina, Maria Craveiro, dá dicas sobre como se preparar a Corrida. — Foto: Unimed Teresina

Quem deseja participar de uma corrida de rua pela primeira vez precisa começar por uma decisão importante: escolher uma distância compatível com seu condicionamento físico. Na Corrida Unimed Teresina 2026 – Amar Rios , marcada para o dia 15 de novembro, os participantes poderão optar entre a caminhada de 3 km e as corridas de 5 km, 10 km e 21 km . Para aproveitar a experiência com segurança, porém, é fundamental respeitar os próprios limites e evitar desafios acima da capacidade física.

A educadora física da Unimed Teresina , Maria Craveiro, explica que a escolha deve considerar a experiência de cada participante com atividades físicas. Para quem nunca correu, a caminhada de 3 km é a opção mais indicada. Já pessoas que mantêm uma rotina de caminhadas e conseguem sustentar um ritmo mais acelerado podem considerar os 5 km, desde que estejam preparadas para o esforço. “Quem nunca correu pode participar, sim. Para essas pessoas, recomendo a caminhada de 3 km. Já quem costuma caminhar em um ritmo mais acelerado pode experimentar os 5 km, respeitando o próprio condicionamento”, orienta.

As distâncias de 10 km e 21 km, por outro lado, exigem maior experiência e preparação específica. Segundo a profissional, quem pretende percorrê-las precisa ter uma rotina regular de corrida e aumentar gradualmente a quilometragem dos treinos. “No caso da meia maratona, o planejamento deve ser ainda mais cuidadoso, com um ciclo de preparação mais longo”, diz Maria.

Reta final: menos intensidade e mais atenção ao corpo

Com a proximidade da prova, a recomendação é evitar mudanças bruscas na rotina de exercícios. Para quem já vem treinando, os últimos dias devem ser dedicados à manutenção do condicionamento, sem exageros. Já quem está começando agora precisa ter expectativas realistas e não tentar compensar a falta de treinamento com atividades intensas na semana do evento.

“Ainda dá tempo de treinar, mas é preciso ter calma e respeitar aquilo que cada pessoa consegue fazer. Quem está começando agora não deve esperar correr 5 km sem parar em poucos dias. O importante é buscar uma evolução dentro das próprias condições”, destaca Maria Craveiro.

Outra orientação é não encarar a corrida como uma obrigação de completar todo o percurso correndo. Intercalar corrida e caminhada é uma estratégia válida, principalmente para iniciantes, pois permite controlar melhor o esforço e recuperar o fôlego durante o trajeto.

“Nem todo mundo que vai fazer os 5 km consegue correr a distância inteira sem parar. Se perceber que está cansando, que o fôlego está ficando curto, pode diminuir o ritmo, caminhar um pouco, respirar e se hidratar. Quando estiver recuperado, pode voltar a correr”, explica.

No dia da prova, um aquecimento leve, com exercícios de mobilidade e ativação muscular, também ajuda a preparar o corpo para a atividade. A educadora física recomenda atenção especial às articulações e à musculatura dos membros inferiores, como joelhos e quadris.

Além disso, os cuidados devem continuar após a linha de chegada. A orientação é reduzir o ritmo gradualmente, manter a hidratação, alimentar-se adequadamente e reservar um período para o descanso e a recuperação muscular. Também é importante evitar exercícios intensos logo após a prova e respeitar os sinais de cansaço do organismo, permitindo que o corpo se recupere antes de retomar a rotina habitual de treinos.

Hidratação é fundamental diante do calor de Teresina

Além do preparo físico, as condições climáticas da capital exigem atenção especial dos participantes. As altas temperaturas e a perda de líquidos pelo suor tornam a hidratação um cuidado indispensável antes, durante e depois da corrida.

Maria Craveiro reforça que não se deve esperar sentir sede para começar a beber água. A reposição de líquidos precisa fazer parte da rotina nos dias anteriores ao evento e continuar durante a atividade, respeitando as necessidades individuais de cada corredor.

“A hidratação não deve acontecer somente no dia da corrida. É fundamental beber água durante toda a semana, porque perdemos muito líquido pelo suor. Durante o percurso, também é importante aproveitar os momentos de hidratação e, depois da prova, repor os líquidos perdidos”, orienta.

A escolha das roupas e dos acessórios também influencia o conforto durante o percurso. A recomendação é utilizar peças leves, calçados adequados e já testados nos treinos, evitando estrear tênis ou equipamentos no dia da competição. Chegar com antecedência e evitar a exposição desnecessária ao sol também são cuidados importantes.

Também é recomendável que pessoas que estão há muito tempo sem praticar atividades físicas, que possuem condições de saúde preexistentes ou que pretendem participar de provas com distâncias mais longas busquem avaliação médica e orientação profissional antes da competição.

“Costumo dizer que quem começa a correr acaba se apaixonando pelo esporte. É uma atividade prazerosa, que proporciona uma sensação muito boa de saúde e qualidade de vida. A pessoa pode começar caminhando, depois correr um pouco e transformar isso em parte da sua semana. É um hábito que pode ser levado para a vida”, pontua a educadora física Maria Craveiro.

A Corrida Unimed Teresina 2026 – Amar Rios será realizada no domingo, 15 de novembro, com concentração no estacionamento adjacente ao Centro Integrado de Saúde Unimed, Unidade Ilhotas, na Rua Monsenhor Gil, 3330.

As inscrições seguem até 11 de novembro, pelo site Piauí Crono ( ). O evento terá caminhada de 3 km, sem caráter competitivo, e corridas de 5 km, 10 km e 21 km.

articles.title: Balsas terão nova operadora e pagamento por Pix e cartões; confira | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova concessionária inicia operação assistida por três meses, sem alteração nas tarifas. Contrato prevê R$ 2,5 bilhões em investimentos e 45 novas embarcações.
articles.summary: Nova concessionária inicia operação assistida por três meses, sem alteração nas tarifas. Contrato prevê R$ 2,5 bilhões em investimentos e 45 novas embarcações.
articles.body:
Travessia de Balsas entre Santos e Guarujá — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/AT

O consórcio AcquaVias SP assume, a partir de segunda-feira (9), a operação de 14 travessias litorâneas no estado de São Paulo. Com a mudança, os usuários também poderão pagar as tarifas por Pix e cartões bancários, segundo a concessionária. Até então, os pagamentos eram feitos apenas em dinheiro ou por meio de tags eletrônicas.

A operação terá um período de transição de três meses, com acompanhamento do governo estadual. Segundo a Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Logística (Semil), não haverá alteração nas tarifas com a entrada da nova concessionária.

A transferência da operação foi anunciada durante um evento no Estaleiro das Travessias de Guarujá (SP), com a participação de representantes do governo estadual e do presidente da AcquaVias, Rodolfo Lima.

Durante os três primeiros meses, a Semil atuará em conjunto com a concessionária, em um modelo de operação assistida que, segundo a pasta, busca garantir a continuidade dos serviços prestados à população.

Além das novas formas de pagamento, o contrato prevê reformas e modernização dos terminais, com melhorias nas condições de embarque e desembarque.

Entre as intervenções previstas estão adequações de acessibilidade, reparos em pisos, coberturas e instalações, além da modernização dos sistemas de informação aos usuários e dos estaleiros.

De acordo com a secretária da Semil, Natália Resende, as obras serão realizadas de forma gradual, conforme as necessidades de cada região e o cronograma estabelecido em contrato.

O projeto também contempla a instalação de infraestrutura de recarga para as futuras embarcações elétricas e melhorias nos sistemas operacionais.

Travessia de Balsas entre Santos e Guarujá — Foto: Arquivo AT

A concessão prevê a aquisição de 45 novas embarcações, sendo 41 elétricas. Segundo a Semil, as primeiras balsas elétricas deverão ser entregues a partir do terceiro ano de contrato.

A substituição gradual das embarcações atuais está prevista para ser concluída até o sétimo ano contratual, quando todas as travessias deverão operar com capacidade plena e as obras de modernização deverão estar finalizadas.

Segundo o governo estadual, a renovação da frota poderá reduzir as emissões de dióxido de carbono (CO₂) em até 18 mil toneladas por ano.

O presidente da AcquaVias, Rodolfo Lima, afirmou que a concessionária está preparada para os desafios ambientais, navais e de engenharia previstos no contrato. “Nós estamos trabalhando firme para que a gente consiga fazer uma boa transição, em nome de todos os usuários”, destacou.

O consórcio AcquaVias SP venceu o leilão das travessias litorâneas em novembro de 2025, ao oferecer um desconto de 12,60% sobre a contraprestação anual média de R$ 461 milhões prevista pelo estado. A proposta superou as de outras três concorrentes.

O contrato, firmado por meio de uma parceria público-privada (PPP), abrange 14 linhas de travessias hídricas no estado de São Paulo, incluindo serviços na Baixada Santista e no Vale do Ribeira. Os investimentos previstos somam aproximadamente R$ 2,5 bilhões.

Além da renovação da frota, o projeto contempla:

Requalificação e ampliação de 20 terminais;

Construção de novas oficinas de manutenção;

Implantação de centros de controle operacional;

Instalação de cabines automáticas de cobrança;

Modernização dos sistemas de automação e segurança.

Os investimentos serão realizados de forma gradual, com a fabricação das novas embarcações e a modernização da infraestrutura existente.

O consórcio AcquaVias SP é formado pelas empresas BK Consultoria e Serviços, Internacional Marítima, Rodonave Navegações, Zetta Infraestrutura e Participações e Innovia Soluções Inteligentes

articles.title: Filhote de elefante-marinho no RS se prepara para o oceano | G1
articles.standfirst: Fêmea ganhou entre quatro e cinco quilos por dia enquanto esteve com a mãe e agora terá de aprender a mergulhar, navegar e buscar alimento.
articles.summary: Filhote nascida na Praia do Cassino permanece sozinha após a mãe voltar ao mar. Animal ganhou até cinco quilos por dia e é monitorado por equipes.
articles.body:
A filhote de elefante-marinho-do-sul que nasceu em Rio Grande , no Sul do RS, no dia 7 de outubro, iniciou uma nova fase de desenvolvimento . Após passar cerca de 20 dias ao lado da mãe, a fêmea agora permanece sozinha na faixa de areia e se prepara para entrar no mar .

A Praia do Cassino foi escolhida pela mãe para o nascimento da filhote e, durante o período em que estiveram juntas, as duas permaneceram próximas, enquanto a fêmea adulta alimentava e preparava a cria para uma nova fase .

Desde que se separou da mãe, a filhote tem aparecido em diferentes pontos da praia e chamado a atenção de moradores e turistas.

"Já estávamos acompanhando esse trajeto dela com a mãe, ficamos sabendo agora que ela estaria sozinha e hoje, através das redes sociais, foi informado que ela estaria aqui, já mais perto. Respeitando o espaço dela, nós decidimos vir aqui conhecê-la", disse a turista Bianca Machado.

A turista Liane Dupont contou que nunca havia visto um animal da espécie pessoalmente.

"E é a primeira vez que eu vejo, assim, pessoalmente. Estou achando muito interessante, né? E admirada, assim, de ver o cuidado com os órgãos de proteção, né?", afirmou.

Segundo os pesquisadores que acompanham o desenvolvimento da filhote, ela ganhou entre quatro e cinco quilos por dia enquanto esteve ao lado da mãe . Cerca de 20 dias depois do nascimento, a fêmea adulta retornou ao mar.

Agora, a filhote terá de desenvolver sozinha habilidades necessárias para sobreviver no oceano .

"Então, agora ela vai aprender sozinha a se alimentar, vai aprender a mergulhar, vai aprender a prender a respiração, a se movimentar e navegar no mar em busca das suas presas", explicou o pesquisador do Ecomega-FURG Renan Costa de Lima.

Equipes do Núcleo de Monitoramento Ambiental (Nema), do Centro de Recuperação de Animais Marinhos e do laboratório de ecologia da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande (Furg) acompanham os deslocamentos do animal para garantir a segurança dele .

A expectativa dos pesquisadores é de que a filhote permaneça por mais algum tempo na região, enquanto aprende e se desenvolve . Conforme Renan Costa de Lima, as pessoas podem observar e fotografar o animal, desde que mantenham distância .

"É uma oportunidade única para todos nós, então é uma coisa que deve ser admirada, aproveitada, mas mantendo esse espaço para o animal se manter tranquilo e fora de qualquer ameaça", afirmou.

Quando estiver preparada, a filhote deve deixar a praia e entrar no oceano. Segundo o coordenador do Núcleo de Monitoramento Ambiental, Sérgio Curi Estima, existe a possibilidade de que ela retorne ao mesmo local.

"Todo o trabalho que foi feito pelas equipes e pela comunidade, essa preocupação, ela conseguiu seguir o seu ciclo natural perfeitamente, então isso é um parabéns para a sociedade aqui, que tem acompanhado também o nascimento deste filhote, que foi histórico na nossa praia", disse.

articles.body: BENGALURU: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Friday said the accused in the Bengaluru family massacre claimed he was humiliated by his wife's family, adding that the killings appeared to have been pre-planned.He said, "It is a very unfortunate incident and looks like it was pre-planned within the family,” news agency ANI reported.“The investigation is on. The accused claims that he was humiliated by his wife's side. It is definitely a twisted mind that has done the job. He has given the whereabouts of the bodies across the state," Kharge added further.The accused, identified as Indushekar, allegedly killed his wife Sunita, mother-in-law Roopavati, brothers-in-law Shivakumar and Shankar, their wives, both named Divya, and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth, police said.According to preliminary findings, the killings took place over two days at the accused's house on 59th Cross, near Bahsyam Circle, in Bengaluru's Srirampura locality. articles.title: Indonesia names fourth wiretapping suspect as political intrigue deepens
articles.summary: Scandal is driving divisions between President Prabowo Subianto and predecessor Joko Widodo.
articles.body:
Indonesian police have named a fourth suspect in a scandal focused on the alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto.

At a news conference late on Thursday, police named a senior law enforcement official with the initials SU as the latest suspect. Three officials were arrested earlier in the week, in a scandal that has exposed a deepening rift between the president and his predecessor – and former ally – Joko Widodo, and sparked security concerns.

Police said that the new suspect served as monitoring chief at Indonesia’s Criminal Investigation Agency between 2010 and 2019. Local media later identified him as Slamet Uliandi.

Investigators alleged that SU, who was the head of the investigation agency’s information and technology unit from 2021 to 2026, gave the go-ahead for the wiretapping.

Cybercrime unit director Suhermanto told a media conference, “When the other two suspects were about to wiretap, they got approval from SU. They also asked his approval before deleting interception records.” Suhermanto added that SU had not yet been detained due to a health condition.

Three senior police officers were arrested on Tuesday, including the former national police chief and Prabowo’s chief of staff, Listyo Sigit Prabowo , who is widely known as a Widodo loyalist.

The case has piled more pressure on Prabowo, with public discontent growing over his costly populist policies and weakening investor confidence in Indonesia’s $1.5 trillion economy.

Police are still investigating the motives behind the attempts to intercept Prabowo’s communications, and have so far questioned 13 police officers and five criminal and IT experts.

The national police chief has also formed a special team to investigate the case, spokesperson Trunoyudo Wisnu Andiko said.

Jakarta remained calm on Thursday and Friday despite the deployment of thousands of troops in the wake of the wiretapping revelations. Military tents and buses were seen in the capital, as well as a small number of soldiers.

Prabowo took office in 2024 after winning the election in a landslide as the continuity candidate for Widodo. Joko Widodo’s son, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, was also elected as Prabowo’s vice president.

Lawmakers are now also considering a probe into the eligibility of Raka in what could be the first step towards removing him from office.

articles.title: How Israel is tightening its grip on Palestinian schools in East Jerusalem
articles.summary: Israeli restrictions on teachers and pressure to adopt Israeli curriculum threaten Palestinian education in the city.
articles.body:
Jamal Shalabi is a 66-year-old chemistry teacher living in el-Bireh, in the occupied West Bank, but since 1998 he has taught in occupied East Jerusalem, making the commute through Israeli checkpoints every day.

The process was tiring, but it allowed him to work. But he now fears that soon won’t be the case, after he was informed by his school’s administration that he was one of 180 Palestinian teachers whose travel permits allowing them entry into East Jerusalem would be revoked upon their expiry at the end of the 2026-27 academic year.

The denial of entry permits to teachers is one of the most prominent restrictions imposed by Israel on schools in East Jerusalem, which, like the West Bank, is illegally occupied Palestinian territory, but which Israel considers part of a unified Jerusalem under its control.

Permits were already a problem for teachers like Shalabi this year, when the issuance of documents was delayed until September 15, two weeks after the academic year began. Permits were also delayed last January. The delays in both January and September led to school strikes in East Jerusalem, a move intended to exert pressure and demonstrate a unified stance against these Israeli measures.

Shalabi explained that even when the permits are approved, they are severely restrictive. The documents can only be used during specific hours, which teachers are not permitted to exceed. The teachers are also prohibited from being anywhere other than the schools.

“These permit restrictions have been in place since the war on Gaza in 2023; we can no longer reach the Al-Aqsa Mosque to pray, nor can we accompany students on school field trips, as the permits are strictly limited to the workplace,” he explained.

“Moreover, for the first time, we were barred from entering Jerusalem for an entire week during the recent Jewish holiday of Sukkot,” he added.

The permit restrictions come alongside wider measures affecting Palestinian education in East Jerusalem, including policies introduced under a plan approved by the Israeli government supposedly aimed at “reducing socioeconomic gaps” in East Jerusalem, whose population is majority Palestinian, despite Israeli efforts to increase the number of Jewish settlers.

The government plan also aims to increase the number of Palestinian students studying the Israeli curriculum. It does so by conditioning funding for new schools on the adoption of the Israeli curriculum, alongside programmes to train teachers within the Israeli education system.

A report by the Israeli human rights organisation Ir Amim warned that the policies exploit educational needs to undermine the autonomy of Palestinian education, as well as its national and cultural identity.

The report further warns of the repercussions of a law that prohibits the employment of teachers who hold university degrees from Palestinian educational institutions, a measure likely to exacerbate the existing shortage of teachers in East Jerusalem’s schools.

According to Ir Amim, approximately half of the education budget allocated under the Israeli government’s plan for East Jerusalem is directed towards expanding the teaching of the Israeli curriculum.

Furthermore, Israeli authorities make the adoption of this curriculum a prerequisite for the opening of new state-funded schools, which the organisation views as a form of pressure on both schools and parents to abandon the Palestinian curriculum.

The number of Palestinian students in East Jerusalem studying the Israeli curriculum was only in the hundreds 15 years ago. But by 2020, the figure had risen to more than 10,000.

The numbers have risen sharply since then. By 2024, it had risen to almost 20,000, according to Palestinian officials, and then to more than 27,000 the following year, according to figures cited by Ir Amim. Palestinian officials estimate that more than 45,000 students – approximately 38 percent of the total student population in the city – are now studying the Israeli curriculum in the 2026-27 academic year.

A principal of a school in East Jerusalem, who requested anonymity for fear of repercussions from Israeli authorities, told Al Jazeera that the expansion of the Israeli curriculum to tens of thousands of Palestinian students is the culmination of years of policies aimed at controlling education in East Jerusalem.

He argued that the situation represents an unprecedented threat to Palestinian education; the imposition of the Israeli curriculum is not merely an academic choice, but a policy designed to forcibly impose a new reality.

“This policy is not limited to official schools affiliated with the Israeli municipality; it also extends to private and community-based schools,” he added. “It involves [an attempt to replace the Palestinian curriculum] with a distorted version printed under the supervision of the municipality that erases and falsifies Palestinian history, geography, and national identity.”

The principal further explained that schools face direct threats, including the loss of funding, financial support, and operating licences if they refuse to introduce classes teaching the Israeli curriculum. This, he explained, was part of an Israeli five-year plan aimed at promoting the “Israelisation” of Palestinian education.

This included strict, rigorous oversight mechanisms, including on-site inspections and monitoring within classrooms, as well as the searching of students’ schoolbags to confiscate original Palestinian textbooks and prevent them from being taught.

“Israeli authorities intervene directly in the appointment of school principals and teachers, revoking the licences of those who don’t comply with their directives. Furthermore, this oversight extends to academic and personal persecution through targeting students, even for their personal social media posts or opinions, and employing disciplinary committees and police summonses to intimidate both staff and students,” the principal explained.

Al Jazeera has reached out to Israeli authorities, but has yet to receive a response.

Schools in East Jerusalem face a deficit of 2,283 classrooms, according to calculations by Ir Amim.

The organisation’s report warns that even if the Jerusalem Municipality’s plans to construct new classrooms are fully implemented, the crisis will not be resolved; a shortfall of approximately 1,100 classrooms is projected to persist by 2032.

For its part, the municipality estimates the current shortage at about 1,500 classrooms, a figure Ir Amim disputes because it says the calculation relies on outdated data.

Ramadan Awad, spokesperson for the Union of Parents’ Committees for Jerusalem Schools, told Al Jazeera that some classrooms contain as many as 42 students.

He explained that the shortage of classrooms is not merely a matter of insufficient space to enrol students; it also creates challenges within the schools themselves. Some institutions are forced to accommodate large numbers of students in cramped rooms, making it difficult for teachers to engage with individual students or monitor their academic progress.

Awad added that some schools have begun seeking out any available building to rent and convert into a school, even if it was originally a residential apartment or a commercial property.

“Such spaces often lack the essential features of a proper school, such as open courtyards, laboratories and rooms dedicated to extracurricular activities,” he said.

articles.title: Lebanese pack bags and stock up amid fears of new Israeli escalation
articles.summary: Lebanese who lived through two Israeli escalations are stocking up and packing bags in case of a third.
articles.body:
Beirut, Lebanon – During Israel’s intensification of its war on Lebanon in March, Aya stayed at her home in Abbasiyeh, in southern Lebanon, despite the risks. At one point, she says, her neighbour’s house was targeted by an Israeli attack.

The attacks have subsided after an ostensible ceasefire was initially announced in April. But the sounds of war have not ceased.

“There’s always drones around and sounds of detonations, but we’ve grown thick skin,” she told Al Jazeera.

In recent weeks, however, fears have intensified around a potential third Israeli intensification since 2024. Many Lebanese are now living in limbo, especially those in areas that previously witnessed intense Israeli attacks.

Aya said her family has prepared extra medication for her grandparents, in case a new round of conflict makes it difficult to obtain. Others are preparing bags and extra food, and keeping their electronic devices charged should the attacks start again.

She also said she would leave her home if Israeli attacks intensified again, rather than stay as she had before.

“I don’t have the energy for this anymore,” she said. Instead, she has been thinking about leaving Lebanon.

“I just can’t handle going through another displacement, especially while watching people around me carry on with their lives as if nothing is happening,” she said. “I know it’s normal, but for me it’s mentally exhausting.”

The Lebanese Shia group Hezbollah and Israel have been at war since October 2023. Since then, Israel has killed around 9,000 people in Lebanon, according to the Lebanese health ministry, mostly during escalations in the autumn of 2024 and in March and April 2026. Israel invaded Lebanon during each offensive and has since occupied up to 10 kilometres of territory , where it has established a so-called “Yellow Line”. Below that line, Israel continues to destroy towns and villages, while it has already made border areas uninhabitable, possibly for years to come .

A ceasefire was announced in April, just over a week after Israel launched more than 100 attacks on Lebanon in less than 10 minutes , killing more than 350 people. Then in June, Beirut and Tel Aviv signed a US-brokered framework agreement to set up “pilot zones”, as part of which the Israeli military would withdraw from those areas and the Lebanese army would move in to disarm Hezbollah.

Following the ceasefire and framework agreement, active fighting between Hezbollah and Israel has eased, despite Israel’s ongoing attacks and destruction of homes and infrastructure in the far south of Lebanon. Those who live above the Yellow Line are mostly out of the line of fire but hear constant explosions and drones, and at times have struggled to access their land .

In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump has reportedly considered launching another round of attacks on Iran, in coordination with Israel. Iran has warned that if such an attack happens, it would retaliate against targets in the region. This has led to questions over whether Hezbollah, which is backed by Iran, would return to conducting its own attacks against Israel.

Israeli officials have also accused the Lebanese army of failing to meet its part of the framework deal – something the Lebanese army denies – in what analysts say might be an effort to build justification for another bombing campaign in Lebanon.

“When it comes to Lebanon, Israel doesn’t need that instigation,” Mohamad Bazzi, a Lebanese political analyst, told Al Jazeera. “It destroyed more of the south under the ceasefire of April 17 than before it. Again and again, Israel has shown its willingness to carry out its policies, to destroy as much of south Lebanon as possible, to make it uninhabitable, and to punish the Shia community and there is no reason it won’t do more of the same if the US and Israel restart the Iran war on a large scale.”

In July 2024, Ramez, who did not want to use his real name for security reasons, was sitting in his bedroom in Beirut’s southern suburb of Haret Hreik when he heard loud explosions. Soon after, the neighbouring building collapsed on his apartment .

Since then, he has stayed in his family’s second home, about a half-hour drive southeast of Beirut.

“The war for me never really stopped,” he told Al Jazeera. “Going to sleep is a gamble between insomnia, nightmares or panic attacks. Even if every country in the world disposed of every single bomb and every single bullet and every single gun, the trauma will stay there.”

He said his family has postponed returning to his home in Beirut’s southern suburbs, known as Dahiyeh, over concerns the attacks could restart. “Personally, I can’t possibly even consider sleeping there without hallucinating the building collapsing in on me again.”

Ramez said he is keeping his batteries and power banks charged, his water supply steady for months and his car’s petrol tank full.

Other people interviewed by Al Jazeera who are from Dahiyeh or the south said they keep go-bags packed.

“People have been planning for a few months,” Karim Safieddine, a non-resident fellow with the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy, told Al Jazeera. “Dahiyeh hasn’t been filled with people in the past few months. At night, it always empties a bit and everyone has a very, very delicate escape route that’s very quick.”

While general anxiety has gripped many in Lebanon over another round of intense fighting, people are also feeling the economic crunch.

The World Bank said in August that it expects inflation in Lebanon to rise to 17.5 percent this year.

And analysts fear that could have severe security consequences.

“As this cycle repeats itself, people get worn down, exhaust their savings and their goodwill, and I think that adds to the possibility of social explosion,” Bazzi said. “Lebanese society will blame Hezbollah for instigating against Israel and by extension [some will blame] the entire Shia community.”

Jad Dilati, a Lebanese analyst from Nabatieh, in southern Lebanon, said that some families have continued to pay rent for apartments in other parts of Lebanon in order “to secure alternative accommodation in case another war breaks out”.

But after three years of war, he said, “that’s a privilege that not everyone can afford”.

Analysts also warned that another round of fighting could increase sectarian tensions in the country. They say Israel has tried to foment internal strife in Lebanon, often by warning non-Shia communities in the south against hosting displaced people. And with people already barely getting by economically, another round of fighting could cause a sectarian spark.

“It is a combustible mix that could explode through something unexpected,” Bazzi said.

articles.title: US judge halts construction of Trump’s triumphal arch in Washington, DC
articles.summary: A 14-day pause has been ordered blocking the so-called ‘Arc de Trump’ project in Washington, DC.
articles.body:
A United States federal judge has ordered a temporary block on the construction of President Donald Trump’s 250ft (76-metre) “triumphal arch” in Washington DC.

US District Judge Tanya Chutkan on Friday, ordered a 14-day pause on any construction on the arch, despite the Trump administration last week saying it could begin as soon as Thursday.

The National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) held a nine-hour hearing on Thursday, which resulted in a final vote of 8-4 in approval of the arch, despite the protest of dozens of witnesses who were against the construction.

Judge Chutkan’s decision follows a series of lawsuits that have been filed challenging the construction of the arch, including a group of Vietnam war veterans, who filed a suit in February.

Trump has proposed building the arch by the Arlington National Cemetery, where war veterans are buried, which caused concerns that it could block the view between the cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial.

The veterans said in a court filing that the line of sight between the two was “carefully designed to symbolise the unification of the country after the Civil War and the strength of a united nation”.

Trump first proposed the arch last year to mark 250 years of US independence, claiming it would be like other famous arches, such as the Arc de Triomphe built in Paris in 1836.

The so-called “Arc de Trump” is only one of many projects Trump has proposed in Washington. On Friday, he signed a proclamation designating his Oval Office and Cabinet room as a national monument.

Many of his plans have been blocked in the past by several judges, and after the Democrats won control of Congress in the midterm elections this week, those plans could face increased scrutiny.

articles.title: UK jailing of Indian sailor over Russia sanctions sets off ‘perfect storm’
articles.summary: Captain Ajay Pant was in international waters when his allegedly ‘shadow’ tanker was captured by British soldiers.
articles.body:
Ritu Pant always made sure that her merchant navy officer husband told her two things before departing on an assignment.

“I always noted the details and the name of his ship and his emergency contact details in case of a crisis,” says Ritu, who is based in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand.

That’s what she did on April 25, when her husband Ajay left Paradip Port in the state of Odisha on board the MT Smyrtos, a crude oil tanker. Her husband had been a sailor for 18 years, and spent six or seven months a year at sea. But growing threats to seamen – amid the wars in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine, and from pirates roaming the high seas – had increased her jitters in recent years.

Yet it was through a social media post that she learned in mid-June that the ship had been captured. Not by pirates, but by the British armed forces, because the MT Smyrtos is under Western sanctions for allegedly working as part of Russia’s shadow fleet, a network of vessels that help Moscow evade United States and European economic restrictions to continue to sell oil and gas, amid the war on Ukraine.

Now Ajay Pant faces charges of flouting United Kingdom sanctions against Russia by commandeering the ship. It’s the first known instance when a European nation has kept a ship captain under arrest on such grounds, and could set a worrying precedent, say lawyers and groups advocating for the rights of seafarers. “This is a unique case,” said Tony Patten, the UK representative at the International Transport Workers’ Federation (ITF), an organisation that works for the rights of seafarers.

Other European countries have also taken over ships that they accuse of violating sanctions against Russia, but while they’ve kept the vessels, they have so far let the sailors go. In March this year, a captain of a suspected Russian shadow fleet was prosecuted in absentia by a French court. In another case from Finland, a court dismissed charges against the captain of a Russian oil tanker accused of damaging undersea cables in the Baltic Sea on account of lack of jurisdiction. In other cases, European nations have set commercial sailors free with fines.

By contrast, Ajay faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted.

The case has also underlined a growing tension between maritime traffic through international waters – the Smyrtos was not in British territorial waters when it was captured – and the enforcement by countries of sanctions that are not approved by the United Nations.

The open seas have always been dangerous, but the risks have mounted as wars and piracy have turned ships and their crew into active targets for militaries and mercenaries alike.

At least 24 seafarers have been killed in the Strait of Hormuz since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. More than 120 commercial ships and tankers have been attacked in this period in the waterway, which used to transport a fifth of the world’s energy supplies before the start of the war.

The death toll in the Black Sea is even grimmer: At least 40 sailors have been killed in more than 570 attacks on vessels there. Piracy off the coast of Somalia has resurged, too.

For Ritu Pant, all of that meant increased insecurity each time her husband went on a ship.“I was quite worried,” she said, describing her thoughts while Ajay was at sea. “When I talked to Ajay, I would tell him that you need to keep in touch always; you need to tell me that you’re fine and everything is safe around because the situation of the sea was very bad.”

But it was not uncommon for her to not hear from her husband for days, due to network disruptions at sea. So Ritu would track updates of her husband’s ship online, a practice that has become increasingly common among families of sailors at sea.

On June 14, the MT Smyrtos was chugging through the English Channel when the Royal Marines Commandos intercepted it, in what was a first-of-its-kind operation authorised by then British Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

At the time, the ship was in international waters, outside the territorial jurisdiction of the UK. Yet Chinook, Merlin Mk4 and Wildcat helicopters from the Maritime Air Group; a Royal Air Force P-8A Poseidon Maritime Patrol Aircraft; a frigate; and a mine countermeasures ship participated in the military operation to take control of the vessel, according to the British Ministry of Defence.

The ship was carrying oil from Russia and was on track to pass through the Suez Canal on its way to India, its destination.

“This successful operation delivers yet another blow to Russia and reminds those fueling Putin’s war in Ukraine that we will not let them hide,” Starmer said in a post on X.

What followed was equally unprecedented; charges of allegedly breaching Russian sanctions were brought against Ajay, who has since been in detention in the UK. After an initial court hearing, his bail was denied.

Enforcement of maritime sanctions brought against Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has been tenuous at best, which makes the Smyrtos case “very unique”, said David Hammond, a lawyer and founder of Human Rights At Sea, a nonprofit and UN-accredited organisation advocating for the rights of people living, working, transiting and operating at sea.

“It is unique in terms of the interception and the interdiction of a vessel that had been sanctioned, having passed through the English Channel as an international transit corridor. It’s, in my understanding, not happened before,” he said.

On the one hand, Hammond explained, the outcome of the case will determine how coastal states enforce sanctions against vessels. But, he said, it also underscores the risks of “criminalisation of seafarers”.

Hammond said Ajay Pant’s case was part of a broader pattern of “shipping crews finding themselves in a position where they are arrested for many crimes, such as trafficking or movement of drugs that they’re not even aware of having been put on board the ship”.

He cited the example of Ali Albokhari, a Finnish-Syrian chief mate on a cargo ship, who was detained by Turkish authorities in 2023 after 137kg (302lb) of cocaine was found on board.

Patten of the ITF echoed similar sentiments. “Our stance is that seafarers being penalised automatically when something like this happens isn’t fair. We would always uphold the right of the seafarer,” he said.

Hammond said Ajay’s case was especially without parallel. “In the case of the Smyrtos, it could be argued that Captain Pant is being criminalised for simply doing his job,” he said, adding that the direction in which the British courts rule will set a new precedent for masters’ accountability over movement of sanctioned goods.

The case, Hammond added, “is a perfect storm in a global storm of impunity; who is accountable and who enforces accountability”.

“And the unintended consequences of which are yet to be seen,” he warned.

The case also raises wider concerns, Hammond said, about how shipping companies and the countries vessels traverse often treat seafarers. “Undeniably, seafarers are seen as disposable assets,” he said, “disposable because they can be easily replaced but concurrently, as assets for assuring continuous global movement of goods by sea.”

The killings in the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea have underscored that sense among sailors and their families – that the lives of those who keep the global economy moving are seen as disposable by those in power.

In a statement shared with Al Jazeera, the International Maritime Organization confirmed at least 66 sailors were killed in various conflicts this year, and hundreds of others injured. Many sailors are also still missing and feared to be dead. “It has been a horrible year for people at sea,” Patten said. “Problems have always existed, but conflicts and geopolitical change have certainly heightened them.”

Ajay Pant’s case also shines new light on a growing number of instances where navies have gone outside their territorial waters to seize tankers that they claim are violating their domestic sanctions regimes.

Since February, when the US and Israel launched their war on Iran, US forces have intercepted and captured several cargo ships in the Indian Ocean. These vessels were seized not just far from US territorial waters but also far from the theatre of their war, on accusations that they were helping Iran evade US sanctions.

The US and the UK argue that they are acting within the bounds of international law.

The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea permits a warship to visit a cargo ship to verify its flag where there are reasonable grounds to suspect the vessel is without nationality. The British Defence Ministry, in its statement after the seizure of the Smyrtos, said that if a vessel is determined to be stateless, the UK can exercise criminal and maritime enforcement powers under its domestic Policing and Crime Act.

The Smyrtos, like many ships that are accused of belonging to Russia’s “shadow fleet”, has frequently changed its flag. The ship had once previously been registered in The Gambia, and then adopted a Cameroon flag in December 2025. When it departed from a Russian port, it had a Cameroonian flag, but Lloyd’s List Intelligence reported that the ship had been removed from Cameroon’s register earlier, in June. It is owned by a Chinese company.

According to the British Defence Ministry, Russia sells about 75 percent of its oil using such shadow tankers.

But whether militaries have the right to enforce their domestic sanctions and laws in international waters against individuals and vessels that are not registered in their territory remains a contested question in international law.

The capture of such vessels raises “a much bigger issue” of “the freedom of navigation at sea”, said Hammond.

To Ajay’s family and those advocating for him, it also raises a more human question: If a cargo ship captain passing through international waters can be captured and tried by nations for allegedly violating their domestic laws, is any sailor safe?

That’s a question that Ritu has lived with in the past few months, forcing the former school principal into advocacy not just for her husband’s release, but for seafarer rights globally.

“Ajay’s case goes beyond just our family, and could be a landmark judgement for seafarers worldwide,” she said. “It raises the fundamental question of whether a master of a ship can be criminalised for decisions that are beyond his authority, knowledge or control.”

The journey has been a difficult one, she said.

“Ajay was the primary breadwinner of his family, and I have also been forced to give up my work to focus on this case,” the mother of an eight-year-old and a one-year-old said.

“He has also been a caregiver to his elderly parents,” she added, saying that for the first few days after the arrest, she kept the news from them, worried for their health. “I wouldn’t allow the daily newspaper in the house and stopped sending my older daughter to school, afraid that someone would say something hurtful to her.”

Eventually, Ritu informed the family and prepared them for the struggles ahead.

“The hardest part is having to do this across continents. We have only spoken to him over short calls, and he has had no personal visitors since I went to meet him in August,” she said. “I don’t want him to feel that he has been forgotten.”

But despite the hardships, she remains hopeful, as support has poured in from the global seafarers community. “When I started posting on social media, I received so many messages from families and wives of sailors,” she said. “Every seafarer’s family I’ve talked to relates to this. So many sailors are getting targeted right now in conflict at sea; they are being made scapegoats.”

Now, she’s preparing for Ajay’s upcoming trial. “I have to bring him back home,” she said. “For his family, but also because no seafarer should be treated in this way.”

articles.title: Court grants ex-Malaysian PM Najib house arrest after $12m royal pardon
articles.summary: Court had approved his transfer after the former prime minister’s party paid $12m fine via crowdfunding.
articles.body:
Malaysia’s jailed former Prime Minister Najib Razak is set to transfer from prison to house arrest after his party paid a $12m fine following a royal pardon.

Najib’s lawyer, Farhan Shafee, told reporters on Friday that he has been given the order and will be “delivering that order to the Kajang prison right now”. His house arrest could start on Friday if everything goes to plan, Shafee said.

However, Malaysia’s attorney general announced on Friday that Najib’s transfer had been temporarily suspended. In a statement, reported by Reuters, the chambers of the attorney general said Najib’s current detention status in prison “will be maintained as some ⁠legal questions regarding the interpretation of ⁠Najib’s conditional ⁠royal pardon ⁠need clarifying”.

Najib, who denies any wrongdoing, has been held in jail since 2022, following his conviction for corruption and embezzlement of billions of dollars connected to 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), a state investment fund he cofounded while in power from 2009-2018.

The order comes after Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim agreed in September to pardon Najib, allowing him to serve the rest of his sentence at home.

Najib’s party, the United Malays National Organisation, has reportedly used crowdfunding to cover Najib’s 50 million ringgit ($12m) fine, as his bank accounts have been frozen.

Al Jazeera’s Rob McBride, reporting from Kuala Lumpur, said this decision could cause a political stir in Malaysia.

“This has an awful lot of political spinoff, potentially impacting the political scene here in Malaysia,” he said. “But also there’s a lot of questions being asked about how the current politics have impacted this pardon.”

He said Anwar Ibrahim, the prime minister of Malaysia, has publicly raised concerns about the pardon within his capacity as the “anticorruption figurehead” in the country. But there has been speculation that he may have, behind the scenes, helped the pardon go through due to pressure from Najib’s party.

Investigators say about $4.5bn was stolen from the 1MDB state fund and more than $1bn of it was linked to Najib.

Najib has said he was solely blamed for a highly complicated global fraud scheme and has denied any wrongdoing.

Separately, he was also convicted in a major 1MBD trial in Malaysia, where he was sentenced to 15 years in prison and a $2.5bn fine for money laundering and the abuse of power.

He has appealed the case and his lawyers requested that the jail term and fines be halted, citing poor health and his inability to pay the fine.

A judge rejected his request in September, saying “the gravity of the offence ⁠is a more important public interest consideration”. Al Jazeera’s McBride said Najib is due to return to jail to serve out this sentence as soon as his house arrest ends in 2028, but it is unclear at this stage if this will happen.
